text: The laboratory results for Patient J indicate a low red blood cell count (3.8 million cells/µL) and a mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 75 fL. An MCV below the normal range (typically 80–100 fL) signifies microcytosis, meaning the red blood cells are smaller than usual. Combined with the low RBC count, this pattern is consistent with microcytic anemia. The most common cause of microcytic anemia is iron deficiency, so further evaluation with iron studies is recommended to confirm this diagnosis.
